FM06.reasoning: The agent trains the model on the full training dataset and predicts on the test set without any internal validation split or cross-validation to evaluate model performance.

FM07.reasoning: The agent uses raw columns as-is with only basic imputation and one-hot encoding, extracting no domain-informed derived features (e.g., total square footage, house age) despite their obvious relevance for housing prices.

other_failure_modes.name: Incorrect ID mapping in submission
other_failure_modes.description: The agent generates submission IDs using a simple range starting from 0 instead of preserving the actual ID column from the test dataset. This will result in an invalid submission file because the IDs will not match the expected test IDs.

other_failure_modes.name: Using ID column as a feature
other_failure_modes.description: The agent includes all columns except the target as features, which inadvertently includes the row identifier ('Id') as a predictive feature, potentially causing the model to overfit to the ID sequence.

summary: The agent implements a basic LightGBM pipeline with proper data imputation and encoding, successfully avoiding data leakage. However, it fails to evaluate the model using a validation split (FM06) and performs no feature engineering (FM07). Critically, it generates incorrect submission IDs by using `range()` instead of extracting the test set's true `Id` column, and it mistakenly includes the `Id` column as a training feature.
